title: Scope, Linkage & Lifetime
html:
Three independent questions about every identifier: where can the name be used (scope), how long does the object exist (storage duration) and can other files see it (linkage).

Scope — where a name is visible

ScopeBegins / endsExample
BlockDeclaration → closing }Locals, loop variables for (int i…)
FileDeclaration → end of translation unitGlobals, functions
FunctionWhole functionOnly goto labels
Function prototypeEnd of the prototypeint f(int n); — the name n

Storage duration — how long the object lives

DurationObjectsLifetimeWhere
AutomaticLocals, parametersUntil the block exitsStack
StaticGlobals, static locals, string literalsWhole program.data / .bss / .rodata
Allocatedmalloc / calloc / reallocUntil freeHeap
Thread (C11)_Thread_localLifetime of the threadPer-thread storage

Lifetime ends while a pointer lives on

Fixes: return the value itself, use a static local, let the caller pass a buffer, or allocate with malloc (caller frees).

Linkage — can other files see it?

External

Globals and functions by default. The same name in every file refers to one object.

Internal

static at file scope. Private to one translation unit.

None

Locals and parameters. Every declaration is a distinct object.

What is the difference between scope and lifetime?

Scope is a compile-time property of a name (the region of source where it can be used). Lifetime is a run-time property of an object (when its storage exists). A static local has block scope but lives for the whole program; a malloced object has no name at all but lives until free.

What is variable shadowing?

Declaring a variable in an inner scope with the same name as one in an outer scope; the inner name hides the outer one until its block ends. It is legal but confusing — -Wshadow warns about it.
